analysis:
Both units are CHANGELOG.md head text only (lines 223-600), so there is no executable code to check. The changelog describes many security-relevant behaviors whose code was not supplied.

Billing and payments (TB-008, A-009):
- New referral rewards at lines 223-228. This is flagged as a threat-model gap.
- Canceled PostgreSQL debit handling at line 238. Lost commit acknowledgements stay uncertain.
- Global Payouts migration and Stripe refund recovery at lines 331-335.

Prompt privacy and cache:
- Line 273 strips top-level user, metadata, safety_identifier and prompt_cache_key from provider-bound bodies. This matches the existing context note that nested content is not anonymized.
- Lines 589-597 keep the SSD cache epoch across eviction and raise the TTL to 30 minutes. Both are already recorded in T-041 as the SEC-035 re-acceptance.
- Line 508 raises the SSD write budget to 750 GB/day. This is a wear and disk-fill change, not a confidentiality change.
- Lines 467-471 add persistence of routing state. It stores only holder and demand metadata, with no prompts or raw chain hashes.
- Lines 273-282 concern cache attempt bookkeeping bounds and SSD hardening.

Provider authorization (TB-005, TB-009, TB-011):
- Lines 291-302 freeze a legacy MDM cohort and require macOS 27+ with App Attest for base rewards. These are described in the canonical context.
- Line 561 notes that the production minimum-version floor needs manual env change.
- Line 567 makes attestation challenges fail closed.
- Line 569 serves App Attest protocol 3 only.
- Line 565 closes T-031 by removing the unauthenticated earnings lookup.

Other:
- Line 327 notes the PR review tooling spend caps and disabled-by-default paid scanning. It is out of the runtime scope.
- Lines 486-498 are deadline and routing changes with no direct security effect.

Integration passes should check the referral settlement code and the actual enforcement of the Privy session requirement. Only the changelog was reviewed, so the code is unverified.

findings.detail: CHANGELOG.md describes a new Open Sales Program. Referrers earn 5% of referred consumers' collected token spend as withdrawable earnings funded by Darkbloom. Settlement is atomic per request, attribution is immutable, and uncertain settlements are retried. This adds a self-service reward-minting path into A-009, the payment ledger, and a new payout path for TB-008. The threat model has no threat for referral-code registration, self-referral or colluding accounts, duplicate or replayed settlement during retry and shutdown reconciliation, or exclusion of owner-routed spend. Only the changelog was visible here, so I could not verify the code. Add a threat entry covering these abuse cases (sybil or self-referral, settlement idempotency, Privy-session enforcement on mutations, owner and self-route exclusions). Add a concurrency and idempotency test for the retry path before relying on the stated mitigations.
findings.title: Referral reward ledger is a new financial surface not covered by the threat model
